battle.name: 第二次英緬戰爭
battle.theater: 仰光至曼德勒伊洛瓦底江流域
battle.brief: 一八五二年三月東印度公司藉駐緬代表遇害與朝儀爭端出兵，四月圍仰光、六月破城，爾後沿伊洛瓦底江北上，一八五六年五月克曼德勒，貢榜王朝覆亡。英軍步兵以雷管步槍為主，底火不受雨霧影響，射程壓過緬軍土砲，開闊地火力即成勝負之別。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries:
第二次英緬戰爭的交戰雙方，是英國東印度公司的印度陸軍連同皇家海軍東印度分艦隊，對上以阿瓦王宮為中心的緬甸貢榜王朝。

英方由三部分組成。其一是東印度公司的印度陸軍：一八五二年三月出兵時只有數個英籍營與數個印度營，到一八五六年攻克曼德勒時，英籍營增至十個上下，印度營三十餘個，另有邁索爾、海得拉巴、特拉凡哥姆、帕蒂亞拉等王公派出的附加部隊，全體掛在英屬印度總督達爾豪斯勳爵與公司陸軍總司令之下，野戰指揮先後交給坎貝爾、戈姆等人。其二是皇家海軍東印度分艦隊：一八五二年由海軍中將查爾斯·拿破倫率領，旗艦為『Sutlej』號，另有『Furious』號等數艘主力艦、巡防艦與汽船，負責封鎖仰光外港與孟加拉灣北岸，並把海軍陸戰隊與水手送上灘頭。其三是技術與後勤人員，由工兵連、造船工、醫生與數百名隨軍勞動者組成，隨大軍沿江北上。

緬方是一個宮廷國家。國王帕賓在位，實權握在其妹蘇帕雅拉與攝政敏基兩派之間。軍隊由王宮直屬的中央部隊，加上阿瓦、勃固、敏建、實皆、丹寧沙利、若開等各省召募的土兵組成，另雇傭數百名外籍傭兵與克倫、沙族部隊。火砲以青銅滑膛口徑二至六磅為主，多無攻城能力；仰光與下緬甸各城由王宮直屬守備部隊與土邦兵分頭防守，糧秣靠牛車與象群走土路輸送。
countriesEn:
The two sides in the Second Anglo-Burmese War were the Indian army of the British East India Company together with the Royal Navy's East Indies Station on one hand, and on the other the Burmese Konbaung dynasty centred on the royal palace at Ava.

The British side had three components. First, the Indian army of the East India Company: in March 1852 it went into the field with only a handful of British and Indian regiments, but by the capture of Mandalay in 1856 the British regiments numbered around ten and the Indian regiments more than thirty, supplemented by contingents sent by the princely states of Mysore, Hyderabad, Travancore and Patiala. All of it hung off the Governor-General of India, Lord Dalhousie, and the company's military command, with field command passing in turn to men such as Campbell and Gomm. Second, the Royal Navy's East Indies Station: in 1852 it was led by Rear Admiral Sir Charles Napier with the 'Sutlej' as his flagship, joined by the 'Furious' and other ships of the line, corvettes and steamers, responsible for blockading the outer roadstead of Rangoon and the northern shore of the Bay of Bengal and for putting marines and bluejackets ashore. Third, the technical and logistic personnel: engineer companies, shipwrights, surgeons and several hundred camp followers, who moved north with the army along the river.

The Burmese side was a court state. King Pagan Min sat on the throne while real power was divided between his sister Supayalat and the regent Mingyi of Ava. Its army was made up of the central troops of the royal palace, plus levies raised by the provinces of Ava, Pegu, Myinsaing, Sagaing, Tenasserim and Arakan, together with several hundred foreign mercenaries and Karen and Shan contingents. Its artillery consisted chiefly of bronze smoothbore pieces of two to six pounds, most of them incapable of siege work; Rangoon and the towns of Lower Burma were held by palace garrison troops and provincial levies in separate hands, and grain and stores moved inland on bullock carts and elephants along dirt roads.
people:
這場戰爭的推手與指揮者分屬兩端。

英方最高層是英屬印度總督達爾豪斯勳爵，他在倫敦與公司商業派的推動下批准接管下緬甸，並在戰事拖長後不斷增兵。真正在野外作戰的是海軍中將查爾斯·拿破倫：他率分艦隊溯江而上，以一次教科書式的砲擊加上強攻奪下仰光，又用緬文公告宣布緬甸歸入英國統治，並懸賞徵募攻佔信號塔的人。英籍陸軍方面，阿奇博爾德·坎貝爾中將自一八五三年接掌遠征軍；他前任布里格迪爾·約翰·安德森率普冒縱隊沿西北山道直取阿瓦，卻在一八五三年四月的亞森加榮敗於摩訶班都拉與紐因揚親王的部隊，安德森不久病故，縱隊折回普冒，成為英軍此後再不敢冒進的教訓。布里格迪爾·戈溫帶領一八五二年仰光至馬爾達本的進軍，其後負責普冒與馬圭方向作戰，一八五五年底向東吁推進時中炮陣亡。亨利·史密斯中校率第一孟加拉歐洲輕步兵團強攻仰光信號塔，隨後成為英軍在緬的一支主力。

緬方由宮廷的兩位主角決定方向。國王帕賓的妹妹蘇帕雅拉掌權，一度與英方秘密往來，希望以合作換取王位與王朝的延續；攝政敏基則主張抵抗。掌兵的摩訶班都拉經驗老到，在克里木與亞森加榮兩役中完勝英軍，卻因屢戰不順與朝中非議而失勢。紐因揚親王後來接掌兵權，一八五五年成為阿瓦朝廷的實際首腦，直到一八五六年曼德勒陷落。
peopleEn:
The men who drove and commanded this war stood at two opposite ends of the field.

At the top of the British side stood the Governor-General of India, Lord Dalhousie, who approved the takeover of Lower Burma under pressure from London and from the company's commercial faction, and who kept feeding in reinforcements as the war dragged on. The man actually fighting in the field was Rear Admiral Sir Charles Napier: he took his squadron up the river, took Rangoon with a textbook bombardment followed by an assault, then issued a proclamation in Burmese announcing that Burma had passed under British rule, and offered a bounty for whoever would carry the Signal Pagoda. The stir this proclamation caused inside the Burmese army was often greater than that of the shells. On the British regimental side, General Sir Archibald Campbell took command of the expeditionary force in 1853; his predecessor, Brigadier John Anderson, led the Prome column along the north-western road to strike at Ava and was beaten at Yenangyaung in April 1853 by the troops of Maha Bandhula and the Prince of Nyaungyan, and Anderson himself died of fever shortly afterwards, the column falling back on Prome and becoming the lesson the British did not forget. Brigadier Godwin led the march from Rangoon to Martaban in 1852 and later fought around Prome and Magway, and was killed by a cannon shot while advancing towards Toungoo in late 1855. Lieutenant-Colonel Henry Smith led the 1st Bengal European Light Infantry in the storming of the Signal Pagoda and afterwards became one of the mainstays of the British force in Burma.

On the Burmese side two figures in the palace set the direction of events. Supayalat, the king's sister, held the real power and for a time carried on secret correspondence with the British, hoping to trade cooperation for the throne and the survival of the dynasty; the regent Mingyi of Ava favoured resistance. Maha Bandhula, who commanded the troops at the opening of the war, was an experienced soldier who beat the British at Krein and at Yenangyaung, yet he fell from favour after repeated reverses and criticism at court. The Prince of Nyaungyan then took charge of the armies and was the effective head of the Ava government from 1855 until the fall of Mandalay in 1856.
kits:
卡面上的雷管步槍是這場戰爭的技術底色。

英軍步兵的標準火器是一八四〇年代換裝雷管的步槍：一八四一年的布蘭斯威克步槍口徑.54，一八五一年制定的恩菲爾德步槍口徑.53，配套的是米涅式小彈；印度各營另有印度式雷管滑膛槍與短管卡賓槍。雷管以底火取代火繩與燧石，扣扳機即擊發，不必先點火再瞄準，也不怕雨霧潮濕——這正是卡面那句話的意思：底火在霧裡也打得響。代價是射程變長，隊形更難維持，隊員之間的間隔一被拉開，前排的射擊就被自己人擋住，於是縱隊行軍的長度、警戒的部署與命令的傳遞速度都成了指揮難題。步槍有效射程約三百碼，開闊地上英軍可以站定射擊，緬軍卻在林蔭下用大鉛彈還擊；這種射程差距，也正是東印度公司據此成立來福槍旅（Rifle Brigade）的背景。

英軍的火力骨幹是砲兵：九磅與二十四磅野戰砲、攻城砲，另有榴彈砲與工兵器材；一八五二年在印度試驗的柯爾特轉輪手槍此時仍屬試裝，未投入緬甸戰場。輸送靠牛車隊、大象與當地平底船，江上另有蒸汽船與海軍內河砲艇分隊。英軍配備挖壕工具、醫療器材與大量備用彈藥，行軍命令規定每兵攜帶六十發子彈。

緬軍裝備明顯落後：火繩槍與燧發步槍仍是主力，另有自一八四〇年代起仿製的.58口徑雷管滑膛步槍，彈丸是大鉛彈，近距離威力驚人，但有效射程短，遠不如英軍精準。火砲多為青銅滑膛二至六磅的小口徑野戰砲，雖有自設鑄砲廠，卻沒有攻城能力，攻擊英軍堡壘只能倚靠人數與接近牆根。緬軍也有戰象與龐大步兵，卻缺乏工程與後勤體系，補給靠牛車與象群走土路，一遇雨季泥濘便寸步難行。
kitsEn:
The percussion rifle on the card is the technical bedrock of this war.

The standard infantry arm of the British army was the percussion rifle adopted during the 1840s: the Brunswick rifle of 1841 at .54 calibre, and the Enfield rifle standardised in 1851 at .53 calibre, fired with the Minié bullet; the Indian regiments carried India-pattern percussion smoothbores and short carbines as well. The percussion cap replaced the match and the flint with a priming charge struck by the trigger, so the soldier no longer had to light a slow match and then take aim, and the weapon did not care about rain, mist or damp: that is precisely what the card means when it says the cap fires in the fog. The price was a longer range, and longer range made formations harder to hold, because once the interval between men was stretched the front rank's shooting was blocked by the men in front of it; the length of a marching column, the disposition of pickets and the speed at which orders travelled all became problems of command. Effective rifle range was about three hundred yards; in the open the British could stand and shoot while the Burmese answered from the shade with heavy lead balls. That disparity in range is also the background to the East India Company's decision to raise a Rifle Brigade.

The backbone of British firepower was the artillery: nine- and twenty-four-pounder field and siege guns, with howitzers and engineer stores. The Colt revolver trialled in India in 1852 was still an experimental weapon and was never taken into Burma. Transport rested on bullock trains, elephants and the local flat-bottomed boats, with steamers and the navy's river gunboat division working the Irrawaddy. The British carried entrenching tools, medical equipment and large stocks of reserve ammunition, and marching orders laid down that each man should carry sixty rounds.

The Burmese equipment was clearly behind the times: matchlocks and flintlock muskets were still the backbone, joined by .58 calibre percussion smoothbores copied from European patterns from the 1840s onwards, firing heavy lead balls that made the weapon devastating at close range but whose effective range was short and whose accuracy was far below the British. Their artillery was mostly small bronze smoothbore field pieces of two to six pounds; although they ran their own foundries, they had nothing capable of siege work, and against a British stockade they could rely only on numbers and on getting close to the walls. The Burmese also had war elephants and very large infantry forces, but no engineering or logistic system of their own; supply moved on bullock carts and elephants along dirt roads, and the moment the monsoon turned the tracks to mud they were rooted to the spot.
tactics:
英軍的戰術框架是線式步兵加砲兵，遇上緬甸叢林便一路打折扣。

在開闊地與緩坡，英軍以二列縱隊行軍，接近敵陣後先展開成線，前排跪姿、後排站姿，雙排射擊，按射擊命令整排齊發。砲兵先行展開，以九磅砲與二十四磅砲壓制緬軍陣線，步兵再以散兵線或密集縱隊前進。程式由鼓號、口令與信號控制，射擊之外還規定一旦四面受敵即組成空心方陣；一八五三年坎貝爾的特別命令把這點寫得很清楚，任何分隊都必須能就地轉成方陣。

叢林把這套東西拆散。道路狹窄、樹冠遮蔽，行軍縱隊被拉長到數公里，前後隊之間視線斷絕，後方部隊聽不到前線槍聲也支援不到。一八五三年四月的亞森加榮是最慘的示範：縱隊在雨季叢林裡被拉成首尾不能相顧的長條，遭到從側翼高地下壓的緬軍切斷，前段被圍殲，後段獨自回撤。教訓是此後英軍不再讓縱隊離開後方掩護範圍，也把偵察、嚮導、糧秣與連續補給線看得比戰鬥本身更重。

攻城方面，一八五二年四月五日英軍完成對仰光的合圍，四月八日強攻信號塔：先以砲火覆蓋山頂，步兵在海軍陸戰隊配合下沿坡攀梯突入，奪下控制全城的制高點，守軍退守城內，圍城延續到六月六日守軍棄城。仰光之外，克里木是英軍第一次在野外頂住數倍兵力進攻的堡壘戰，守軍以圓形方陣與火網消耗進攻方，圍攻方終因傷亡與糧秣耗盡退去。

緬軍的戰術完全相反：避免在開闊地與英軍正面對射，盡量在叢林、山脊與雨季泥路中遲滯英軍縱隊，切斷糧道，襲擊落單的補給隊與哨所，必要時焚毀沿線村莊與積穀，使英軍失去就地取食的機會；同時以小股兵力不斷試探英軍防線，找到方陣與縱隊之間的縫隙再集中打擊。

海軍方面，分艦隊在孟加拉灣封鎖海岸、攻擊河口要塞，內河砲艇與蒸汽船沿伊洛瓦底江推進，用船載砲射擊兩岸堡壘，並為陸上縱隊指示方向、補充彈藥。英軍遠征到曼德勒，靠的就是海軍先沿江建立據點，再由陸上縱隊接手。
tacticsEn:
The British tactical framework was line infantry supported by artillery, and the Burmese forest knocked it down at every step.

In open ground and on gentle slopes the British marched in two columns, deployed into line as they neared the enemy, the front rank kneeling and the second standing, firing in double rank and discharging the volleys on the firing order. The artillery deployed first, using nine- and twenty-four-pounders to crush the Burmese line, and the infantry then advanced either in skirmish order or in close column. The drill was controlled by drums, orders and signals, and besides the prescribed volleys there was the standing rule that a unit attacked on all sides should form a hollow square; Campbell's special order of 1853 put it plainly, every detachment must be able to turn into a square on the spot.

The forest pulled all of this apart. The tracks were narrow, the tree canopy shut out the sky, the marching column was drawn out over several kilometres, and the line of sight between the head and the tail of the column was broken: the troops in the rear could neither hear the firing ahead nor reach it. Yenangyaung in April 1853 was the worst demonstration: the column was stretched into a long string in the jungle of the wet season, cut by Burmese troops coming down from the high ground on its flank, the leading part surrounded and destroyed while the rear withdrew on its own. The lesson was that the British afterwards kept columns within reach of their supporting troops, and came to value scouting, guides, commissariat and a continuous line of supply more highly than the fighting itself.

In siege work, on 5 April 1852 the British completed the investment of Rangoon and on the 8th stormed the Signal Pagoda: artillery first swept the summit, then infantry, supported by marines, climbed the slope and forced the crest that commanded the whole town, the garrison falling back inside the walls, and the blockade dragging on until the defenders evacuated the city on 6 June. Outside Rangoon, Krein was the first time the British stood in the field against a fort being assaulted by several times their number: the garrison used a circular square and a belt of fire to grind the attackers down, and the besieging army eventually withdrew, worn down by losses and by the shortage of food.

Burmese tactics were the exact opposite: avoid meeting the British in the open, and instead delay their columns in jungle, on ridges and on the muddy tracks of the wet season, cut the roads, fall on isolated supply parties and picket posts, and where necessary burn the villages and the grain along the line so that the British could not eat off the country. Small bodies of troops probed the British line continuously, looking for the gap between a square and a column, and concentrated their strength on the point they found.

On the naval side the squadron blockaded the coast of the Bay of Bengal and attacked the river-mouth forts, while the river gunboats and steamers worked up the Irrawaddy, carrying guns that fired at the forts on either bank and directing and resupplying the columns on land. It was on this pattern that the British expedition reached Mandalay: the navy first established its bases along the river, and the land columns took over from there.
data:
時間與數字可以對照戰報重排。

一八五二年一月二十五日，東印度公司的駐緬代表亨利·伯尼在阿瓦宮外遇害，案子指向宮廷勢力；三月一日英方就朝廷禮節提出最後要求，戰事隨即在三角洲展開。四月五日英軍包圍仰光，四月八日奪下信號塔，六月六日守軍棄城，緬方失去海港。八月二十九日克里木之戰，緬軍以約一萬人圍攻約兩千人的英軍堡壘，攻不下，援軍抵達後解圍。

一八五三年三月三十一日梅達梅之戰，坎貝爾率約二千二百人迎擊約六千至八千名緬軍，勝出。四月五日至九日亞森加榮，約一千三百人的英軍縱隊遭重創，損失過半，是英軍在這場戰爭中最慘重的失敗。

一八五四年，英軍兩度派隊嘗試打通比莫通往雲南的商路，在孟養與八莫一線受阻撤回；同期緬軍與清軍在雲南邊界交戰，另一條戰線成形。一八五五年英軍在東吁方向與阿瓦朝廷反覆爭奪普冒、馬圭與東吁三處據點，戈溫中將陣亡。一八五六年五月二十九日戈姆的縱隊進入曼德勒，王宮被佔；九月王室被移交英方看管，錫包成為名義國王。一八五七年二月《揚達波條約》簽訂，戰事以條約收尾。

數字方面：英軍先後投入的兵力約二萬至三萬人，英籍營最終約十個；仰光至曼德勒陸路約九百五十公里，沿伊洛瓦底江上行的水程約一千公里，仰光距海約一百六十公里；恩菲爾德步槍口徑.53，有效射程約三百碼（約二百七十公尺），緬軍常用步槍口徑.58；行軍命令規定每兵攜帶六十發子彈。損失方面，克里木之戰英軍損失有限，亞森加榮一役英軍縱隊損失超過一半，仰光信號塔強攻英軍傷亡以百計，佔出擊兵力相當比例。
dataEn:
The dates and the figures can be rearranged from the dispatches.

On 25 January 1852 Henry Burney, the East India Company's resident at Ava, was murdered outside the royal palace, and the trail pointed into the court. On 1 March the British delivered their last demand on the question of court precedence, and the fighting opened at once in the delta. The British invested Rangoon on 5 April, carried the Signal Pagoda on the 8th, and the garrison evacuated the city on 6 June, costing the Burmese their seaport. At the battle of Krein on 29 August the Burmese brought about ten thousand men against a British garrison of roughly two thousand, failed to take the stockade, and withdrew when the relieving force arrived.

At Maingpyin on 31 March 1853 Campbell led about two thousand two hundred men against a Burmese force numbered at six to eight thousand and won. From 5 to 9 April came Yenangyaung, where a British column of about thirteen hundred was mauled and lost more than half of its strength, the worst defeat the British suffered in this war.

In 1854 British columns twice attempted to open a trade route through Bhamo to Yunnan and were checked on the Myinsaing and Bhamo line and withdrew; at the same time Burmese and Qing troops fought along the Yunnan frontier, and a second front took shape. Through 1855 the British and the Ava government fought repeatedly for Prome, Magway and Toungoo, and Brigadier-General Godwin was killed. On 29 May 1856 Gomm's column entered Mandalay and the palace was occupied; in September the royal family was placed under British guard and Sibawpaw became king in name. In February 1857 the Treaty of Yandabo was signed and the war was closed by treaty.

On the figures: the British committed something in the order of twenty to thirty thousand men over the course of the war, ending with about ten British regiments; the road from Rangoon to Mandalay runs about nine hundred and fifty kilometres, while the water route up the Irrawaddy is about a thousand kilometres, and Rangoon stands some one hundred and sixty kilometres from the sea; the Enfield rifle was of .53 calibre with an effective range of about three hundred yards, roughly two hundred and seventy metres, while the common Burmese musket was .58; marching orders laid down that each man carried sixty rounds. On losses: the British cost at Krein was limited, the Prome column at Yenangyaung lost more than half of its number, and the storming of the Signal Pagoda cost the British casualties numbering in the hundreds, a substantial share of the force committed to the assault.
cause:
打起來是幾件事疊在一起。

一八二六年《揚達波條約》之後，緬甸割地賠款，被限制對外通商，只能與英國私人商號交易；東印度公司卻要打通經緬甸通往廣州的陸路茶絲道，也要取得柚木林的開採權，兩邊在稅則與港口管治上越來越僵。一八四〇年代後期起，英國機織棉布大量湧入緬甸，本土手工業受衝擊，宮廷以限制進口、拒絕英國人設廠來維護本國工匠，收入因此更少，怨氣更重。

一八五二年一月二十五日，東印度公司的駐緬代表伯尼在阿瓦宮外被殺，案子指向宮廷中的勢力。緊接著是位次之爭：英方要求緬方在外交場合把英國代表排在緬臣之前，等於要阿瓦朝廷向英國低頭；一八五二年三月一日英方期限一到，東印度公司即以恢復秩序為名出兵三角洲。

英方另有一層動機：法國在越南與雲南一帶的影響力正在上升，緬甸是通往中國內陸的門戶，若落入法國手中，東印度公司就會失去進入雲南的唯一陸路。也正因如此，英國要的不是一個親英的緬甸王，而是一個聽話的、由自己扶持的緬甸王。宮廷內部蘇帕雅拉一派與攝政敏基一派的角力，讓原本還能談判的事迅速變成兵事。
causeEn:
The war came out of several things coming together.

After the Treaty of Yandabo of 1826 Burma had ceded territory and paid an indemnity, and was restricted in its external trade, being left to deal with British private merchants alone; the East India Company, for its part, wanted to open an overland tea and silk road through Burma to Canton and to obtain the right to work the teak forests. The two drifted further apart over tariffs and over who should govern the ports. From the late 1840s large quantities of machine-woven British cotton cloth poured into Burma, hitting local handicrafts, and the court answered by restricting imports and refusing to let British subjects set up mills, in order to protect the country's own craftsmen; revenue fell further, and the resentment grew.

On 25 January 1852 Burney, the company's resident in Burma, was killed outside the palace at Ava, and the trail pointed into the court. What followed was the question of precedence: the British demanded that their representative should take rank over the Burmese ministers on all occasions of state, which amounted to requiring the court of Ava to bow to Britain. When the British ultimatum of 1 March 1852 expired, the East India Company marched into the delta in the name of restoring order.

There was a further motive on the British side. French influence in Vietnam and around Yunnan was growing, and Burma was the gateway to the interior of China; if it fell to France the East India Company would lose its only land route into Yunnan. For that reason what Britain wanted was not a Burmese king friendly to Britain but a Burmese king who would obey, a puppet of its own making. The struggle inside the palace between Supayalat's faction and the regent Mingyi of Ava turned a dispute that might still have been negotiated into a campaign of arms.
impact:
這場戰爭把緬甸從獨立王國改造成英國殖民地，也改變了東南亞的權力格局。

仰光陷落後下緬甸即由英方民政接管，一八五六年攻克曼德勒後上緬甸也被併入英屬印度，貢榜王朝的行政機構、稅制與土地制度被逐步替換，柚木開採與對外貿易由英方特許公司經營。一八五二年十一月英方強迫阿瓦朝廷簽訂商約，開放仰光、毛淡棉、丹寧沙利等口岸，廢除緬甸對進出口的壟斷與關稅上限，並派駐代表常駐宮廷；此後大批印度契約勞工被運入緬甸，上緬甸的清剿一直延續到一八八五年英國兼併全境。

軍事上，這是英軍在亞洲少數以雷管步槍打完的最後幾場大型戰爭之一。射程優勢在開闊地極為有效，叢林裡卻幾乎用不上，英軍自此更重視工程、後勤與通信；英屬印度陸軍也在實戰之後討論米涅小彈造成的創傷，一八五四年成立專用來福槍旅，一八五〇年代中期則試用柯爾特轉輪手槍，下一場大規模用兵時英軍已改用後膛針發槍。

對英國自身而言，戰爭證明在亞洲用少量歐洲軍加大量印度軍、以商路與航線為目標的遠征方式可行；但比莫通往雲南的商路兩次嘗試都沒能打通，英國的注意力因此轉向雲南，並在數十年後演成中英之間的一連串糾葛。對緬甸社會而言，王權覆亡之後宮廷不再是國家中心，寺院、施主與地方菁英填補了空缺，佛教的傳播與政治結黨反而在往後數十年裡更形活躍。
impactEn:
This war turned Burma from an independent kingdom into a British colony and rearranged the balance of power in South-East Asia.

Lower Burma passed to British civil administration as soon as Rangoon fell, and Upper Burma was absorbed into British India after the capture of Mandalay in 1856; the administrative machinery, the taxation and the land system of the Konbaung dynasty were progressively replaced, and the working of the teak forests and the foreign trade were handed to chartered companies. In November 1852 the British forced a commercial treaty on the court at Ava, opening Rangoon, Tavoy, Mergui, Tenasserim and other ports, abolishing the Burmese monopolies and tariff ceilings, and stationing a British representative at court. Large numbers of Indian indentured workers were afterwards brought into Burma, and the pacification of Upper Burma ran on until the British absorbed the whole country in 1885.

Militarily this was one of the last large wars the British fought in Asia with the percussion rifle as their standard arm. The advantage of range was decisive in the open and almost useless in the jungle, and the British turned their attention more towards engineering, logistics and communication; the army in India also debated, in the light of what it had seen, the wounds inflicted by the Minié bullet, raised a dedicated Rifle Brigade in 1854, and experimented with the Colt revolver in the middle of the 1850s, going into the next large war with the needle breech instead.

For Britain itself the war proved that an expedition in Asia could be fought with a small number of European troops and a large number of Indian troops, directed at trade routes and lines of communication; but the trade road through Bhamo to Yunnan could not be opened in two attempts, so British attention turned to Yunnan and, some decades later, produced a long series of quarrels with China. For Burmese society, once the monarchy had gone the palace was no longer the centre of the state; monasteries, donors and local gentry filled the gap, and the spread of Buddhism and its political organisation became more active in the decades that followed.
result:
結果很明確：英國全勝，緬甸滅國。

一八五六年五月二十九日英軍進入曼德勒，王宮的武器庫與財產被清點，帕賓與蘇帕雅拉在九月移交英方看管，錫包在名義上接替王位。一八五七年二月《揚達波條約》簽訂，緬甸正式成為英屬印度的一個省，上緬甸割讓給英國，貢榜王朝被廢除，國王與王室成員被押往印度安置，宮廷土地充公，割讓區維持英軍佔領，直到一八八五年全境兼併。

軍事收尾沒有停在曼德勒：緬軍餘部退入北部山地，英軍在往後十餘年以分遣隊方式肅清普冒、曼德勒周邊與西北山區；比莫商路仍然沒有打開，英軍轉而尋求經雲南通往中國內陸的道路。戰後的東南亞因此出現兩條長線：一條是英國在緬甸的殖民統治，另一條是英國在雲南與法國爭鋒的通道問題，而後者最終在二十世紀初化為衝突的源頭。
resultEn:
The outcome is plain: complete British victory, and the end of Burma as an independent state.

On 29 May 1856 the British entered Mandalay; the palace armoury and treasure were inventoried, and in September Pagan Min and Supayalat were handed over to British custody, Sibawpaw taking the throne in name. With the Treaty of Yandabo of February 1857 Burma became formally a province of British India: Upper Burma was ceded, the Konbaung dynasty was abolished, the king and the royal family were taken to India and settled there, the palace lands were confiscated, and the ceded territory remained under British military occupation until the whole country was absorbed in 1885.

The military conclusion did not stop at Mandalay. The remnants of the Burmese army withdrew into the northern hills, and for more than ten years afterwards the British cleared Prome, the country around Mandalay and the north-western districts with flying columns. The Bhamo trade road was still not opened, and the British turned instead to seeking a road to the Chinese interior through Yunnan. South-East Asia after the war therefore showed two long lines: British colonial rule in Burma on one hand, and on the other the question of the corridor into Yunnan where Britain and France would contend, a question that was to become the source of conflict in the early twentieth century.
